source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text:
This source gives specific numeric maturity windows for durian and describes several physical maturity-check methods farmers use together to judge readiness, since relying on a single sign can be misleading.

Days-based estimate: this source cites roughly 106-108 days from flower opening to maturity for one described variety, and roughly 112-113 days for another, similar in principle to Source A's variety-specific day counts but with different specific numbers -- since these counts come from different source documents describing possibly different varieties or orchard conditions, growers should treat both sets of day-counts as approximate reference points to be confirmed against physical maturity signs on their own trees, not as fixed universal numbers.

Physical maturity checks described in this source: stalk color and texture change (the stalk nearest the fruit becomes drier and slightly discolored as the fruit approaches maturity); the ridges between spine sections becoming more clearly defined as the flesh fills out and separates slightly from the husk wall; the tapping sound test (tapping the husk and listening for a change from a dense, solid sound to a slightly hollow or duller sound as the flesh separates from the husk); and a specific-gravity / float test, where a mature fruit's density changes as internal air pockets develop with ripening, so some growers test whether a fruit floats or sinks in water at a particular orientation as a supplementary maturity indicator. The source recommends using at least two of these signs together rather than relying on any single one.
